unverified_facts: Titanis walleri lived in the Pliocene to early Pleistocene, roughly 5 to 2 million years ago.
The species name honors Benjamin Waller, who found the first fossils in the Santa Fe River, Florida.
Titanis fossils are known from Florida and Texas.
Titanis stood about 1.9 m (6 ft) tall; older estimates were up to 2.5 m (8 ft).
Titanis belongs to the phorusrhacids (terror birds), most of which lived in South America.
Terror birds reached North America during the Great American Biotic Interchange.
Whether Titanis mainly hunted or scavenged is debated.
